comparator.name: Business Administration
comparator.route: Management in the Digital Age specialisation with its associated thesis
comparator.sourceNotes: The official 2026–27 curriculum accounts for exactly 180 EC. Years 1 and 2 each comprise ten 6-EC components spanning strategy, economics, organisational behaviour, research methods, quantitative and qualitative analysis, operations, accounting, marketing, finance, information and data management, international business, law, ethics and entrepreneurship. The second-year restricted choice is instantiated as Innovation Management because it coheres with the formally selected third-year Management in the Digital Age specialisation; this is a route-coherence choice rather than a UCR-fit choice. Year 3 preserves 30 EC of genuine minor, study-abroad, internship or elective space, followed by an official 30-EC specialisation-and-thesis block. The public curriculum does not provide a reliable credit split inside that combined block, so no thesis credit is invented.

alternatives.label: Business, management and entrepreneurship
alternatives.concept: A broad business-administration route combining entrepreneurship and strategy with accounting, finance, economics, marketing, leadership, organisational behaviour, research, data and international business.
alternatives.labelReason: The completed programme spans strategy, economics, marketing, finance, organisational behaviour, entrepreneurship and research, matching the broad business-administration identity.
progression: Business, economics, data and research foundations precede advanced strategy, law, leadership, econometrics and market research; all formal prerequisites occur earlier and every course is offered in its assigned term.

alternatives.label: Business, sustainability and responsible management
alternatives.concept: A business route organised around sustainable business strategy, circular operations, responsible leadership and sustainable marketing while retaining core management, economics, research and legal foundations.
alternatives.labelReason: Corporate responsibility, responsible decision-making and sustainable business are direct recurring programme themes, supporting a management curriculum with a strong sustainability centre.
alternatives.distinctness: Compared with the closest match, this route replaces much of the general economics, data, communication and technology mix with a sequenced sustainability curriculum focused on climate, circularity, governance, renewable systems and sustainable operations.
progression: Sustainability Essentials I precedes Sustainability Essentials II, which precedes advanced circular-resource and renewable-system work; business and research foundations precede advanced law, public economics, leadership and market research, with all formal prerequisites completed earlier.

alternatives.label: Finance, accounting and business decision-making
alternatives.concept: A finance and analytics route combining accounting, finance and economics with econometrics, probability, data science, machine learning, programming and optimisation for business decision-making.
alternatives.labelReason: Corporate finance, Accounting and Control, Finance, financial management, financial accounting and management accounting form an explicit coherent route.
alternatives.distinctness: Compared with the broad closest match and the sustainability route, this curriculum substitutes mathematics, programming, databases, optimisation, probability and additional economics/finance for much of the leadership, marketing, communication and sustainability content.
progression: Programming and mathematical methods precede decision algorithms, linear algebra and probability; economics and research foundations precede advanced economics, econometrics, finance and market research, with all formal prerequisites completed earlier and all courses offered in their assigned terms.

candidates.label: Digital innovation and new ventures
candidates.reason: The official digital-management and entrepreneurship directions support another coherent concept, but production stops after the three stronger broad, responsible-business and finance/control alternatives.

routeSelection.route: Management in the Digital Age specialisation with its associated thesis
routeSelection.basis: Among the four formal third-year specialisations, Management in the Digital Age most broadly continues the programme-wide identity in strategy, organisation, people, information, data and digital transformation. Accounting and Control, Finance, and Entrepreneurship, Innovation and Creativity are narrower functional routes. The route is selected before comparing UCR courses.

selection.assessment: The closest route covers the broad business-administration core. Direct target evidence then supports a responsible and sustainable-business programme and a finance/accounting/control programme. All three are feasible 24-course curricula and satisfy the pairwise four-course distinction rule. Digital innovation and entrepreneurship are separately supported, but production stops at the maximum of three.

blocks: UvA requires dedicated management accounting; UCR's finance/accounting route provides adjacent financial decision-making but no identical course.
UvA requires a dedicated qualitative-research project; UCR distributes qualitative and applied research across courses.
The official restricted Innovation Management choice supports the selected digital-management route.
UvA combines international business law and ethics in one compulsory course.
The genuine 30-EC open semester is preserved without invented content.
UvA's selected specialisation and thesis are published as one 30-EC block; UCR has no identical formal block.

notes.text: UvA Business Administration requires a broad two-year sequence across business functions and methods, then 30 EC of open choice and a formal 30-EC specialisation-and-thesis block. UCR can assemble broad-management, responsible-business and finance/analytics programmes, but it does not reproduce UvA's combined specialisation-and-thesis structure or every dedicated accounting, operations and international-business component.
